visualMethod: Qualitative editorial examples of noticing, responding and leaving room. No quantities, scores or causal estimates.

meaningEvidence: Original TikTok video and matching Threads cross-post visually show the same toddler, paving, stones and toy vehicle.
English audio clearly compares children with real-life Pokemon; uncertain closing words are not quoted.
Original caption frames a playful parenting moment with humorous level, energy and obedience scores.
Narrator identity is not independently established. The article attributes the Pokémon narration to the clip and first-person publication/commentary only to the verified post and caption.
limitations: The brief scene establishes no developmental outcome, exact age or general family routine.
Article commentary expands the clear playful theme without inventing a personal event.
Posting-account identity does not establish who recorded the narration, the child’s identity or a parent-child relationship. These are not inferred.
